title: Three Nevada aftershock gaps reject independent times with a threefold six-hour density cap
abstract: We derive a sharp probability bound for two independent event times with a capped density. We apply it to a previously tested first USGS aftershock forecast region in Nevada. Three six-hour bins each contain two records, and all three gaps are at most 10 minutes. Any independent-time model with arbitrary within-bin shapes and density at most three times each bin mean has a joint tail bound of 0.00407470. An eight-sequence correction gives 0.03259763. The sharp critical cap is 3.484238 times the six-hour mean. The result permits non-monotone rate shapes and correlated mixtures of profiles. It strengthens an existing daily smooth-rate bound on the same snapshot; it is not independent confirmation. Raising the magnitude threshold removes the Nevada rejection. This post hoc result constrains recorded-event rate explanations, but does not identify secondary triggering or establish forecast skill. Code, proof, source hashes, aggregate evidence and a figure are included; external record-level inputs remain separate.

display.caption: Sharp eight-sequence probability bound for three two-event bins, and their observed short-gap totals. The horizontal line is 0.05. This is a conditional model bound, not a confidence interval for a physical rate.
